scenarios.name: Stretch the opening
scenarios.note: The desired flat extent changes from two to six shared steps at beat four.

scenarios.name: Shrink the flat extent to zero
scenarios.note: The desired flat extent becomes zero. Zero-length phases and their separate sites remain present.

scenarios.name: Increase the separation
scenarios.note: The desired vertical reach changes from two to four shared steps.

scenarios.name: Two pressures together
scenarios.note: The flat extent and the vertical reach both increase. Separate exposed roles carry the two requests.

scenarios.name: Change the goal again
scenarios.note: The requested flat extent increases to six, then falls to one at beat twelve.

scenarios.name: Temporarily missing signal
scenarios.note: The follower's comparisons are absent on beats four through nine, then resume.

scenarios.name: Temporarily ambiguous signal
scenarios.note: The follower admits all three comparison outcomes on beats four through nine. These are alternatives, not three commands.

scenarios.name: Signal never returns
scenarios.note: The follower receives no comparisons after beat three. An evaluator can still inspect its actual state, but that state does not repair the missing channel.

scenarios.name: Three-beat-old comparison
scenarios.note: The follower receives each comparison three beats late. Its sign was correct when observed; it may be stale now.

scenarios.name: The receiver cannot stretch far enough
scenarios.note: The follower's flat-extent capacity is three while the desired extent becomes six. Each admitted request remains accounted for.

scenarios.name: Two incompatible desired extents
scenarios.note: On alternate beats, a second supplied goal asks the follower for flat extent one. The other beats ask it to agree with the first pen.

scenarios.name: A smaller goal after blocked growth
scenarios.note: The follower first accumulates blocked growth at capacity three. At beat twelve the desired extent becomes one; old tension is not erased.

scope: Authored native comparison/response machines and paired drawing templates. Bounded whole-step extent correction; no image fitting, discovered topology or universal geometric settlement.

retention.scope: Supplied hold/clock/feedback laws; two different directional challenges, not repeated samples of one test. A native gate retains a candidate archive only after both public comparisons settle from unequal to equal. This selects an existing coupling policy; it does not discover a new law, an ornament topology or its construction history.

candidates.reason: At least one challenge remained unequal, missing or ambiguous; no candidate is installed by default.
